html:
A man made famine in Soviet Ukraine in 1932 and 1933, caused by the policies of Joseph Stalin's government. Millions of Ukrainians died; most estimates run from about 3.5 to 5 million. The name means "killing by hunger".

It grew out of forced collectivisation, which wrecked farming. The state still set very high grain quotas for Ukraine and kept seizing grain when harvests fell short. Villages that failed to deliver were blacklisted and cut off from goods. In January 1933 peasants were barred from leaving Ukraine and the Kuban to look for food.

Famine also struck other grain regions, and in Kazakhstan the Kazakh famine killed a larger share of the people. What marks Ukraine is the evidence that measures were aimed at it in particular while Ukrainian culture and leaders were also under attack.

The Soviet Union denied the famine for decades. Since independence Ukraine has commemorated it, and Ukraine and many other countries recognise it as a genocide. Some historians dispute that label, but not the scale of the deaths or the state's role.
sum: A man made famine in Soviet Ukraine in 1932 and 1933, caused by the policies of Joseph Stalin's government. Millions of Ukrainians died; most estimates run from about 3.5 to 5 million. The name means "killing by hunger".
